claims.statement: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in drug discovery has profoundly transformed the pharmaceutical landscape by significantly accelerating the identification of potential drug candidates.
Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have proven to be particularly effective in modeling molecular structures, optimizing drug-target interactions, and enhancing prediction accuracy.
Graph neural networks can be applied to drug discovery.
Graph Neural Networks are used in modern AI-aided drug discovery.
Graph Neural Networks can be applied to drug discovery.
An integrated decision support pipeline based on Graph Neural Networks has been developed for drug discovery.
Molecular generative Graph Neural Networks can be used for drug discovery.
Graph neural networks can be used for automated de novo drug design.

gaps.description: Standard benchmark datasets for drug‑discovery GNN research (e.g., MoleculeNet, ChEMBL, PDBbind) are never used in the existing claims.
evidence: Datasets used in claims: none detected
Expected datasets never used: ChEMBL, MoleculeNet, PDBbind, PubChem BioAssay, ZINC15

gaps.description: The literature contains virtually no empirical studies on molecular property prediction (e.g., solubility, toxicity, bioactivity) using graph neural networks.
There is a lack of methodological comparisons and baseline reporting across major GNN variants (MPNN, GCN, GAT) for drug‑discovery tasks.
evidence: Claims per method: Message Passing Neural Networks (MPNN)=0, Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) and Graph Attention Networks (GAT)=0

gaps.description: There is a complete absence of work on protein–ligand interaction modeling and binding affinity prediction with GNNs.
evidence: Protein–ligand interaction modeling and binding affinity prediction =0

gaps.description: No studies have applied graph‑based generative models (e.g., GraphVAE, MolGAN) for de novo molecular generation and optimization in drug discovery.
evidence: De novo molecular generation and optimization using graph-based generative models =0

gaps.description: Evaluations are limited to generic claims; there is no real‑world, prospective, or longitudinal validation of GNN‑based drug‑discovery pipelines.
evidence: Sample claims are generic statements without quantitative results or real‑world validation
